html:
The Northern Wintu are the northern branch of the Wintu, a people of the upper Sacramento, McCloud and Trinity rivers in northern California, around Mount Shasta and today's Redding. The McCloud River had great salmon runs, and Wintu villages caught and dried salmon and gathered acorns.

From the 1850s the Gold Rush brought miners, massacres and disease that killed most Wintu. In 1872 the US built a salmon hatchery on the McCloud, and Wintu people worked there. Shasta Dam, finished in 1945, flooded the lower McCloud with its villages and sacred sites and ended the salmon runs above it. The Winnemem Wintu, the McCloud River band, have since campaigned to bring the salmon back. See also Nom Ti Pom, Kl'bal Pom and their southern neighbours the Patwin.
